1.0.0.en: The Apostle Peter sends his greetings to the believers in Asia Minor and throughout the world, to everyone from among the Gentiles who believed and received this grace, like the Jews who believed, of whom Peter was one. This one precious faith is a grace from Christ, the righteous and holy Saviour of the whole world. In humility Peter joins his old name "Simon," meaning God hears, to his new name "Peter," meaning the rock, and he describes himself as a servant of Christ and not only His apostle, for he does not forget that he was merely an uneducated fisherman, and that it was Christ who raised him up and made him a great apostle.

1.1.0.en: The Apostle Peter's wish for the believers is an abundance of peace and grace through the knowledge of God and of Christ the Redeemer. Here he repeats what Christ Himself said: "And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent" (Jn 17:3).

1.1.1.en: Encourage everyone you meet with words of grace, love and peace, so that you reassure all amid the troubles of the world.

1.1.2.en: (2) Spiritual striving (vv. 3-15:) 3 According as his divine power hath given unto us all things that pertain unto life and godliness, through the knowledge of him that hath called us to glory and virtue: 4 Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust. 5 And beside this, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge; 6 And to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience; and to patience godliness; 7 And to godliness brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness charity. 8 For if these things be in you, and abound, they make you that ye shall neither be barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ. 9 But he that lacketh these things is blind, and cannot see afar off, and hath forgotten that he was purged from his old sins. 10 Wherefore the rather, brethren, give diligence to make your calling and election sure: for if ye do these things, ye shall never fall: 11 For so an entrance shall be ministered unto you abundantly into the everlasting kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.

1.1.3.en: 12 Wherefore I will not be negligent to put you always in remembrance of these things, though ye know them, and be established in the present truth. 13 Yea, I think it meet, as long as I am in this tabernacle, to stir you up by putting you in remembrance; 14 Knowing that shortly I must put off this my tabernacle, even as our Lord Jesus Christ hath shewed me. 15 Moreover I will endeavour that ye may be able after my decease to have these things always in remembrance.

1.2.0.en: When we have come to know Christ and believed in Him, the Holy Spirit grants us every possibility of the spiritual life through the sacraments of the Church. In Baptism we receive a nature inclined to become like God, and He establishes us in it through the Holy Myron; if we sin, He forgives our sins in the sacrament of confession and nourishes us with His most holy Body and Blood; indeed He shepherds and guides us in His Church through the means of grace. And through the calling to life with Christ, God is glorified in us so that we may live by the spiritual virtues.

1.3.1.en: Exceeding great promises: the promises of the Old Testament and the promises of Christ to those who believe in Him, which the Holy Spirit grants them.

1.3.2.en: Partakers of the divine nature: the new nature that we receive in Baptism, our union with Christ in the sacrament of the Eucharist, and the permanent indwelling of the Holy Spirit in us.

1.3.3.en: The work of the Holy Spirit in us gives us glory and virtue through the Holy Sacraments, which lift us up to share in God's nature as far as we are able to bear it. By this spiritual elevation in the Christian life we keep away from the evil lusts that corrupt the souls of the people of the world, and we enjoy purity in our lives.

1.4.0.en: For this very reason: to receive the spiritual life, the promises and the participation in the divine nature that grace grants us.

1.4.1.en: If grace gives us the possibilities of life with Christ, then we must respond to it with spiritual striving and diligence, so that our faith produces spiritual conduct and virtues; and as we live by virtue, we experience God and know Him in practice.

1.5.0.en: The Apostle continues his discourse on the stages and degrees of the spiritual life, which is a chain in which each link leads to the next, and he says:

1.5.1.en: To knowledge temperance: when I experience God and love Him, material things become small in my eyes, so I control myself in using them and am content with little of them; that is, I practice temperance toward them.

1.5.2.en: To temperance patience: and when I control myself in material things, in emotion and in all earthly matters, the ability to be patient and to endure is formed within me, so I am no longer disturbed by any afflictions. To patience godliness: while I am patient in afflictions and restrain myself from desires for God's sake, His mercies and consolations pour out upon me as divine help, which helps me toward a life of godliness with all that it includes: repentance, the fear of God, clinging to Him and delighting in fellowship with Him.

1.6.0.en: He continues his discourse on the stages of the spiritual life in this chain, and says:

1.6.1.en: To godliness brotherly kindness: when a person fears God and lives in repentance and a spiritual relationship with Him, he is satisfied with Him, so he is freed from his selfishness and opens himself to others, and is able to build good relationships with them and to encourage them.

1.6.2.en: To brotherly kindness charity: by speaking kind words and encouraging others, the heart opens in love toward them, and my love for them confirms and increases my love for God and my faith in Him, so I walk in the virtues through which I know God. And so I find that the chain in its end leads back to its beginning, or that any part of it leads to another and makes me grow spiritually.

1.7.0.en: These spiritual stages urge a person on with zeal to know God, and his life is filled with spiritual fruits, which are the virtues and the various kinds of service.

1.8.0.en: On the other hand, the one who neglects these spiritual steps and the striving in them is described by the Apostle as blind, or at least as having weak spiritual sight, because he has forgotten the grace he received in the renewal of his nature and in leaving his old sins, since he ought to have grown in the new life with God, and his lack of striving exposes him to returning to his old sins.

1.9.0.en: The Apostle urges us to stand firm in the faith to which God called us and in which He chose us to be His children, and this by spiritual striving in all the preceding steps, for by this striving and by holding fast to the faith we protect ourselves from falling into various sins or returning to our old evil life.

1.10.0.en: He encourages us to hold fast to spiritual striving, because by it we walk in the way of the Kingdom and its gates are opened to us so that we may enjoy eternal happiness.

1.11.0.en: Therefore the Apostle Peter does not neglect to remind them of spiritual striving, although they know it and are established in the faith in Christ in whom they live, because this reminder makes them grow in spiritual striving.

1.12.0.en: The Apostle sees that he is responsible to remind them of spiritual striving because he feels that his life on earth is drawing to its end. He compares his life to a dwelling or tent whose removal is near, so that he may move to another place, which is the blessed eternity, and he charges his children not to be negligent in their striving after he leaves them and goes to Christ.

1.12.1.en: Be careful in your striving against your favorite sin, and know that any effort you offer is precious to God, and He will support you in it so that you experience it in practice, in addition to your being freed from your sin.

1.13.s.en: (3) The Transfiguration and the prophecies prove the divinity of Christ

1.13.0.en: The Apostle Peter declares that he did not base his preaching on fables he had heard or on stories that men had invented, but that he had himself beheld the power of Christ and His divinity in His life on earth and in events that show His divinity, such as His transfiguration on the mountain.

1.14.1.en: The Apostle Peter affirms the divinity of Christ and His greatness by the glory and honor He received at the Transfiguration, when the Father called to Him from heaven, where the great glory is, saying to Him, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased" (Mt 17:5). Peter, together with James and John, heard the voice of the Father from heaven when they were with Christ on the mount of the Transfiguration.

1.15.0.en: A light that shineth: he compares the prophecies to a shining lamp.

1.15.1.en: A dark place: the Old Testament, when humanity was far from God and from knowing Him.

1.15.2.en: The day ... the day star: Christ, when He became incarnate in the fullness of time so that the prophecies would be fulfilled in Him. He directs their attention to the prophecies about Christ in the Old Testament that prove His divinity; they are like the light of God in the midst of the darkness of humanity's ignorance in the Old Testament, until they were fulfilled in Christ by His Incarnation and redemption.

1.16.0.en: What the prophets recorded in their prophecies was not a human effort to interpret events, but was by inspiration of the Holy Spirit.

1.17.0.en: No prophecy ever came by the will of man, and these prophets did not speak from themselves or according to their own inclinations, but spoke moved by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit.

1.17.1.en: Read the words of the Holy Bible with reverence, knowing that they are the voice of God to you, that you may live by it and apply it in your daily life.

2.0.s.en: (1) The appearance of the false teachers

2.0.0.en: The Apostle Peter reminds them of the false prophets who misled the kings and the people in the Old Testament so that they would not listen to the words of God's prophets, as happened in the days of King Ahab (1 Kgs 22:22). Likewise now there are false teachers who proclaim heresies by which they reject the divinity of Christ, who bought us with His blood; so they and those who follow them are far from salvation, and nothing awaits them but eternal torment.

2.1.0.en: These false teachers claim to be Christians although their doctrine is mistaken, so they mislead many of the people and lead them to destruction, and because of these heresies they confuse the thoughts of the pagans about Christianity, so that they speak evil of it.

2.2.0.en: They trade in souls, despising the precious blood that was shed for them, and deceive the hearts of the simple with kind words and smooth, deceitful speech; therefore judgment pursues them, and their destruction does not delay or slumber.

2.2.1.en: Be careful about what you hear or read, and if you find it different from what you have learned in the Church, be on your guard and ask your father of confession, so that you are not led astray by strange teachings that resemble the sound teachings.

2.3.0.en: The Apostle makes clear the justice of God, who punishes those who persist in their wickedness, such as the false teachers. And he gives three examples of His justice:

2.3.1.en: The first example: His punishment in ancient times of the angels who became proud and fell and were sentenced to eternal torment; He bound them and prevented them from returning to their first rank and from enjoying fellowship with Him, and they are now awaiting their eternal torment. If His mercy did not prevent His justice toward the fallen angels, then it does not prevent His punishing the heretics either.

2.3.2.en: Chains of darkness: the bonds of their sin, which prevent them from enjoying fellowship with God.

2.3.3.en: Hell: the place where the wicked wait, but they can war against human beings with God's permission.

2.3.4.en: Reserved: waiting and bound, not enjoying the sight of God until the day of judgment comes. Judgment: the day of judgment, which transfers them to eternal torment.

2.4.0.en: The second example of God's justice is that He spared not the old world in the days of Noah, who preached righteousness and they did not respond to him, so God brought a flood upon them because of their ungodliness; yet He preserved Noah, who was one of eight persons who were saved from the flood, namely he, his wife, his three sons and their wives.

2.5.0.en: The third example of His justice is His sentence of destruction upon the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah because their wickedness had increased and the cup of their iniquities was full; so He turned them into ashes, making them an example to everyone who lives an ungodly life in every generation and persists in evil without repenting.

2.6.0.en: Alongside God's justice, His mercy appears in His care for His children; He did not forget Lot and his two daughters, because he did not mingle with the wicked in their uncleanness, but was greatly distressed by the conduct of these wicked people.

2.7.0.en: For as Lot, a righteous man, dwelt among them, his soul was grieved every day by the shameful perversions in their conduct, which he saw and heard of.

2.8.0.en: He concludes from the preceding verses that God is able to deliver His righteous children from the afflictions of life and to keep them in their upright faith, whereas the wicked He puts in hell, the place where the wicked wait until the day of judgment, to enter into eternal torment. For God is perfect in His mercy to His children and in His justice toward the wicked.

2.8.1.en: Do not despise God's longsuffering and mercy and so persist in your sins, but use it for repentance and for staying away from sources of evil, for your attempts at repentance are very precious in God's eyes however weak you are, and He is ready to support you and, in the end, to lift your sins from you.

2.9.s.en: (3) The characteristics of the false teachers

2.9.0.en: Dominion: the Lord Christ and the authority of the Church represented in the Apostles and their successors the bishops. Dignities: the angels.

2.9.1.en: The Apostle declares that God's punishment is severe for the false teachers, who have evil characteristics, the most important of which are:

2.9.2.en: 1- Uncleanness: by being carried away into the lusts of the flesh and evil sexual perversions.

2.9.3.en: 2- Pride: they rise up with their heresies against Christ Himself and against the Church, her shepherds and her teachers, proclaiming strange ideas; they are bold in ungodliness and evil, and boast of their pride to the point of speaking evil words against the angels.

2.10.0.en: The righteousness of the angels appears in their not condemning the demons or these heretics, since they leave judgment to God, and we ought to imitate them.

2.11.0.en: 3- Ignorance: he compares them to unreasoning, predatory beasts, made to be caught and killed by men, for these false teachers have sunk to a rank lower than the animals, instead of preserving their rational human dignity. And although they are ignorant of the angels, they invent judgments and slanders about what they do not know; so just as the unreasoning animals perish, they too perish like them, and the cause of their destruction is not outside them but is their own corruption.

2.12.0.en: 4- Delight in lusts: the false teachers are occupied with material desires and take pleasure in them, although they are temporary and are followed by eternal punishment, and they are also characterized by many other evil traits such as vanity.

2.12.1.en: 5- Hypocrisy: they pretend to be godly and take part in the love feasts with the members of the Church and try to cause them to stumble with their mistaken ideas.

2.13.0.en: 6- The evil gaze: because their hearts are full of uncleanness, their eyes look about seeking defilement, so they are adulterous eyes.

2.13.1.en: 7- Deceit: they are not content with doing evil, but try to influence the simple and unstable in order to deceive and mislead them.

2.13.2.en: 8- Covetousness: they have fallen into the love of possessing and are absorbed in lusts with all their hearts. And since they have these evil characteristics, God's punishment, His curses and eternal destruction come upon them.

2.14.0.en: 9- Love of money: these false teachers were members of the Church who walked uprightly, but they loved their lusts and perversions, so they sought material things, like the prophet Balaam, who loved material gain and caused the children of Israel to stumble so that they departed from God and their enemies defeated them (Num 22-25).

2.15.0.en: The ignorance of the false teachers appears like that of Balaam, who was warned to turn back from his evil by his donkey, which spoke with a human voice to rebuke him (Num 22:28-30).

2.16.1.en: The blackness of darkness: intense darkness.

2.16.2.en: He affirms the hypocrisy of these wicked people, comparing them to wells to which the thirsty person comes and finds no water in them, or to clouds that the farmer waits for to rain and water his crops, but the winds drive them away and he benefits nothing from them. And he states again that after this life eternal destruction awaits them, which is expressed by intense darkness.

2.17.0.en: The great things of falsehood: innovations and heresies.

2.17.1.en: 10- Varied stumbling blocks: they proclaim many heresies, and whoever of the believers rejects them, they try to bring down into unclean lusts and fornication in order to draw him away from God.

2.18.0.en: 11- False freedom: they imagine that indulgence in lusts is freedom, and in misleading others they promise them this false freedom, but in truth it is slavery to sin. And if they are slaves to sin, how can they free others, since they themselves first need to repent of their sins in order to be truly free?

2.19.0.en: 12- Returning to sin: these false teachers received purity when they believed in Christ and left behind their former evil lusts, but they returned to them and plunged even more deeply into them, so that the last end of their life is worse than before their faith, because after they were enlightened they rejected Christ and preferred evil.

2.20.0.en: Their knowledge of the new life in Christ condemns them. Had they not known it, they would have some excuse, but now their judgment is greater.

2.21.0.en: He quotes a verse from the Book of Proverbs (Prov 26:11), comparing the false teachers to a dog that vomits and then, after being cleaned, returns again to its vomit, so it remains filthy and no one can come near it because of its smell and its repulsive appearance. He also compares them to the swine, which after being washed returns to its bad habit of wallowing in the black mire, so that its whole body becomes dirty. So these wicked people return to their evils as if they did not know Christ or the pure life that is in Him.

2.21.1.en: God accepts your repentance however great your sins, but do not be negligent and return to the encouragements of sin and forget all the blessings you received in life with God; remember the judgment and the eternal torment that await the wicked, so that you flee from sin.

2.21.2.en: Faith in God and readiness for His second coming
